key_insight: Mac-Diff combines conditional diffusion with a locality-aware cross-modal attention mechanism to generate diverse conformational ensembles for unseen proteins, capturing both dynamic flexibility and structural heterogeneity in a single generative framework.
problem_solved: Existing structure prediction approaches often produce single static models and fail to represent the range of biologically relevant conformations; Mac-Diff addresses the challenge of generating diverse, realistic conformational ensembles conditioned on input modalities for proteins not seen during training.
method: Conditional diffusion generative model that stochastically samples protein conformations conditioned on input modalities (e.g., sequence and structural cues).
Locality-aware cross-modal attention aligns information across modalities while emphasizing neighborhood (local) interactions to preserve realistic local geometry during generation.
Training on known structures/ensembles and using the diffusion reverse process to produce diverse, physically plausible conformers for unseen proteins.
impact: Introduces transferable modeling components (conditional diffusion + locality-aware cross-modal attention) that advance generative modeling of biomolecular ensembles and can be applied to other conditional diversity-sensitive tasks in AI/ML, improving downstream design and simulation workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline schematic: conditional diffusion forward/reverse process with input modalities (sequence, structural cues) and ensemble outputs.
Diagram of locality-aware cross-modal attention showing alignment between modalities and focus on local neighborhoods.
Protein ensemble overlay: multiple generated conformers superimposed on a reference to illustrate structural diversity and flexibility.
Bar/line chart comparing ensemble diversity and fidelity metrics vs baseline methods (e.g., RMSD distribution, coverage of known states).
paper_title: Conditional diffusion with locality-aware modal alignment for generating diverse protein conformational ensembles
paper_authors: Baoli Wang, Chenglin Wang, Jingyang Chen, Danlin Liu, Changzhi Sun
